newsitem.title: ESTONIA: LEKS TALKS WITH PARTNER FOR BALTIC EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: LEKS TALKS WITH PARTNER FOR BALTIC EXPANSION.

text.p: Leks Insurance, which has launched a share issue and wants to list its shares on the stock exchange, has held negotiations to include a foreign strategic investor to help it enter the Baltic market, it said on Tuesday.
Leks yesterday started subscriptions for a share issue to raise its capital by four million kroons to 42 million kroons.
"The plan is to start cooperation to go to the Baltic market," sales director, Tarmo Karma, told Reuters.
"We are looking for a partner for know-how and professionalism," he added.
"Leks does not rule out the possibility (to include a strategic investor) and does not confirm it is going to happen in the short-term," Karma added.
Karma said Leks has had negotiations with insurance companies from western Europe but did not name them.
The strategic investor will not become a major shareholder in Leks, he added.
A major shareholder in Leks with some 52 percent in the company is Estonia's fourth largest bank, Tallinna Pank.
